security_audit.summary: All 51 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, SQL identifiers, multilingual text, and documentation examples. No prompt injection, hidden executable payload, or obfuscation was found. Operational examples can still delete or overwrite data without explicit confirmation safeguards.

remediation.issue: Destructive database and overwrite examples lack an approval boundary.
remediation.suggestion: Require an explicit user confirmation, validated scope, backup, and dry run before delete, overwrite, cleanup, or production deployment operations.

remediation.issue: The JDBC example places credential placeholders directly in source code.
remediation.suggestion: Use environment-backed secret references or platform secret managers, and state that generated code must never contain real credentials.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Operations Lack Confirmation Safeguards
semantic_findings.description: The command reference includes a database delete, and the PySpark template uses overwrite mode. The skill does not require confirmation, backups, or dry runs before these actions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both destructive patterns are explicit examples, and surrounding guidance directs the agent to deploy and run pipelines. Risk depends on access to live systems.

semantic_findings.title: Inline Credential Pattern in JDBC Example
semantic_findings.description: The JDBC example places username and password values directly in pipeline code. Although placeholders, this pattern can encourage users to embed real credentials.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The username and password options are visibly embedded in the example. They are placeholders, so no actual secret exposure is present.

content.user_title: Build Reliable Data Pipelines and Warehouses
content.value_statement: Data teams need practical guidance for building dependable pipelines across complex platforms. This skill designs, implements, tests, and troubleshoots batch, streaming, warehouse, and lakehouse workflows.
actual_capabilities: Designs batch and streaming architectures for databases, APIs, logs, message queues, object stores, warehouses, and lakehouses.
Produces PySpark jobs, Flink SQL, Airflow DAGs, dbt models, table definitions, and pipeline configuration guidance.
Defines warehouse layers, dimensional models, partitions, storage formats, incremental loads, and change-data-capture strategies.
Creates data quality checks for completeness, accuracy, consistency, uniqueness, timeliness, and source-to-target reconciliation.
Diagnoses Spark skew, memory pressure, Kafka lag, Flink backpressure, slow SQL, small files, and storage capacity issues.
Plans metadata, lineage, access controls, masking, retention, monitoring, alerting, and operational documentation.
limitations: The skill provides guidance and examples; successful execution requires configured tools, credentials, connectivity, and platform access.
Example hostnames, table names, dates, credentials, resource sizes, and retention settings must be replaced and reviewed.
Generated designs require validation against actual data volume, service limits, compliance rules, and recovery objectives.
Delete, overwrite, cleanup, and production deployment actions need explicit approval and tested rollback procedures.

use_cases.title: Build a Production ETL Pipeline
use_cases.description: Design an incremental source-to-warehouse pipeline with transformations, scheduling, quality checks, monitoring, and recovery steps.

use_cases.title: Model an Analytics Warehouse
use_cases.description: Create layered tables, dimensions, facts, dbt models, tests, documentation, and partition strategies for reliable reporting.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Data Platform Failures
use_cases.description: Analyze runtime evidence and produce prioritized fixes for Spark, Kafka, Flink, Airflow, HDFS, or SQL performance problems.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Warehouse Model
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new analytics domain
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a warehouse model for [business domain]. Identify source tables, facts, dimensions, grain, keys, partitions, quality checks, and open questions.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Incremental ETL Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an incremental pipeline from [source] to [target] using [orchestrator]. Include idempotency, retries, backfills, validation, monitoring, and rollback steps.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Streaming Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Kafka to Flink to [sink] pipeline for [event type]. Cover schemas, partitions, watermarks, state, checkpoints, delivery guarantees, and observability.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a Production Bottleneck
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these [Spark, Flink, Kafka, Airflow, or SQL] metrics and logs: [evidence]. Rank likely causes, tests, low-risk fixes, and validation criteria.

output_examples.input: Design a daily incremental MySQL to ClickHouse order pipeline.
output: Architecture: Airflow schedules a partitioned extraction and stages records before an idempotent ClickHouse load.
Controls: Track a durable watermark, deduplicate business keys, reconcile counts, and quarantine invalid records.
Operations: Add retries, failure alerts, backfill parameters, latency metrics, and a documented rollback procedure.

output_examples.input: Diagnose a Spark job where a few tasks run much longer.
output: Primary hypothesis: skewed join keys create oversized shuffle partitions.
Validation: Compare task input sizes, shuffle reads, executor time, and key-frequency distributions.
Actions: Test adaptive skew handling, broadcast the small side, or salt confirmed hot keys.

output_examples.input: Plan data quality checks for an orders model.
output: Check order identifiers for uniqueness and required fields for completeness.
Validate amounts, statuses, timestamps, and foreign-key relationships against accepted business rules.
Reconcile source and target counts, monitor freshness, and block downstream publication on critical failures.

best_practices: Provide data volume, latency, source schema, target platform, deployment environment, and recovery requirements before implementation.
Test pipelines with representative data and verify counts, checksums, schemas, freshness, resource use, and restart behavior.
Store secrets outside code and require explicit approval before destructive or production-changing operations.
anti_patterns: Do not apply example credentials, hostnames, dates, resource settings, or retention policies directly to production.
Do not optimize from assumptions alone; collect execution plans, runtime metrics, logs, and data-distribution evidence first.
Do not run deletes, overwrites, full refreshes, or cleanup commands without backups, scoped validation, and rollback plans.

faq.question: Which data platforms does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers common Spark, Flink, Kafka, Airflow, dbt, warehouse, lakehouse, query, quality, and governance workflows.

faq.question: Can it generate implementation artifacts?
faq.answer: Yes. It can draft pipeline jobs, SQL models, DAGs, table definitions, tests, configurations, diagrams, and operational guides.

faq.question: Can it run pipelines automatically?
faq.answer: Execution depends on the connected agent tools and your environment access. Review commands, credentials, targets, and change scope before running them.

faq.question: Does it support both batch and streaming systems?
faq.answer: Yes. It addresses scheduled ETL, incremental loading, change-data capture, Kafka pipelines, Flink processing, and Spark Structured Streaming.

faq.question: How should production credentials be provided?
faq.answer: Use your platform secret manager or protected environment references. Never place real passwords, tokens, or keys in generated source files.

faq.question: What evidence helps with performance troubleshooting?
faq.answer: Provide execution plans, job metrics, stage timings, partition sizes, logs, data volumes, schemas, resource settings, and recent changes.
